headline: M23 has held the Rubaya coltan mines since 30 April 2024
detail: UN investigators say the armed group occupies Rubaya town and the whole surrounding coltan mining area, and controls the routes from there into Rwanda.

headline: At least US$800,000 a month for M23 from one mining area
detail: The UN Group of Experts estimates M23 collected this from taxing coltan production and trade at Rubaya in 2024, with around 150 tonnes a month smuggled across the border into Rwanda.

headline: Rwanda's coltan excess tracks what Congo's Kivu provinces stopped recording
detail: Rwanda exported about 760, 1,040 and 1,440 t more coltan than its geology predicts in 2023–25, while official Kivu output fell 490, 910 and 1,350 t below its earlier level. Our central estimate is that 50–85% of the excess could have come from armed-group-held areas. Net growth shipped to China.
method: Excess uses a tin-ore baseline frozen at 2022–24 for 2025. Shares apply 50/75/100% pass-through rates, which are our judgement, to UN volumes. No source states these shares.

headline: Sanctions have hit the refinery, the army and a bank — not the coltan exporters
detail: Since 2025 the US and EU have sanctioned Rwanda's gold refinery, its army, its defence ministry and a military savings bank. None of the seven Rwandan coltan exporters that Global Witness links to Rubaya has been designated.
method: Comparison of the OFAC and EU designation lists (2025–Oct 2026) against the exporters named by Global Witness (Jun 2026).

headline: Conflict gold still reached Kigali's refinery a year after EU sanctions
detail: The US Treasury says at least 60 kg of gold from M23- and army-held areas of South Kivu moved through Rusizi to Gasabo Gold Refinery in early 2026, about a year after the EU listed the refinery.

headline: Eight Rwandan exporters have strong or moderate evidence and no sanctions
detail: Mixing UN and NGO reports, customs records and open registries grades 20 unsanctioned exporters and traders. Four exporters rest on a UN report plus a second organisation. Customs and registry data reveal owners and networks, but every armed-group link still rests on UN or NGO evidence. Most of them deny the claims or did not reply.

headline: 41 major companies list smelters named in the coltan chain
detail: All eight smelters were conformant under the industry audit scheme in May 2026, and six of those statuses have been frozen since RMI paused China assessments. A listing means a smelter may be in a supply chain; no filing says a company received Rubaya material.
